India Names Bhaker and Sehrawat as Flagbearers for Aichi-Nagoya 2026

India has officially announced Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat as its flagbearers for the opening ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games. The selection designates the decorated shooter and prominent wrestler to lead the Indian contingent into the stadium, highlighting the nation’s focus on established medal contenders.

This dual choice underscores the breadth of India’s athletic representation across distinct disciplines. Both athletes have consistently performed on the international stage, making them symbolic figures for the upcoming event in Japan. The organizers have emphasized cultural performances and advanced technology for the ceremony, though specific financial allocations for the production were not disclosed in the official announcement.

The Aichi-Nagoya Games are set to be a critical target for Indian athletes aiming to secure top finishes. The presence of high-profile flagbearers is expected to boost team morale and draw significant domestic attention. As the event approaches, attention will turn to whether these high expectations translate into strong performances during the two weeks of competition.

The opening ceremony will serve as the official start of one of the largest sporting gatherings in Asia, bringing together athletes from across the continent. While the event has not yet commenced, preparations are in their final stages to ensure a smooth launch for the global audience.

IIT Bombay student found dead; police investigate after exam phone violation

A student was found dead in their hostel room at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay, authorities confirmed. Local police have initiated a preliminary investigation to determine the specific circumstances surrounding the death. An inquest has been conducted, and the body was released to the family following standard legal procedures.

According to an official statement from the institute, the student had been previously caught using a mobile phone during an examination. This violation of academic regulations resulted in disciplinary action. The institute stated that the student was aware of the pending disciplinary proceedings based on this incident. However, the source material does not establish a direct causal link between the phone incident and the death. Police are currently reviewing digital footprints and interviewing close acquaintances to piece together the timeline of events leading up to the discovery.

The IIT Bombay administration expressed regret over the incident. A committee has been formed to review the situation and ensure that student welfare protocols are adhered to in the future. The institute emphasized that while academic integrity is paramount, the well-being of students remains a priority. Counseling services have been made available to the broader student community. The university is cooperating with law enforcement agencies to ensure a thorough inquiry. No other students or staff members have been implicated in the incident at this stage.

Source: The Hindu

ABVP Takes Early Lead in DUSU Elections After First 15 Rounds

Vote counting for the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections began at 8:00 AM today. Security personnel maintained a perimeter around counting centers to oversee the process.

Preliminary results from the first fifteen rounds indicate that Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidates are currently leading for both the President and Secretary positions. The National Students' Union of India (NSUI) trails in these categories.

In the Vice-President race, independent candidates are currently topping the polls. This distinguishes the VP contest from the leadership races, where the two major student political wings are the primary contenders.

At the Sri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), ABVP candidates secured all available seats. No similar sweep was reported for NSUI or independent candidates in this specific college during the initial count.

Official results are still pending as the remaining votes are tallied. University election officials have not yet declared final winners for any position. The complete data release will determine the final margins and the composition of the student leadership.

The counting process continues under the supervision of designated election observers. No disputes have been formally recorded during the first phase of the count. The final declaration will follow once all college-level results are aggregated and verified.

Source: News18 India

Lord Rees Warns AI Is Already Displacing White-Collar Roles

Lord Martin Rees, the former Astronomer Royal, has intervened in a House of Lords debate to highlight immediate labor market shifts driven by artificial intelligence. Speaking in June 2026, Rees argued that the technology is no longer a distant threat but is currently supplementing or replacing specific white-collar tasks. He cited this ongoing integration as evidence that regulatory frameworks are overdue, rather than merely precautionary.

The debate challenged generic discussions about future risks by focusing on present-day economic displacement. Rees emphasized that AI systems are already altering employment structures in knowledge-based sectors. This tangible impact, he noted, requires specific legislative attention to manage workforce transitions and maintain human oversight.

Beyond employment, Rees raised concerns about the stability of highly interconnected AI networks. He warned that without strict controls, these complex systems could exceed human management capabilities, posing distinct challenges to societal stability. His remarks shifted the focus from abstract safety theories to concrete operational risks and labor data.

His intervention underscores a growing urgency for policymakers to move beyond broad principles. Instead, they must develop robust mechanisms that address the specific, measurable effects of AI on the current workforce and system integrity.

What to watch: Concrete legislative proposals addressing white-collar job displacement and AI network stability.

Source: News18 India
